brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A clonal, mid-leaf, mid-season tea cultivar of small tree habit, bred at the Wuxi tea variety institute in Jiangsu and listed as a national improved variety. It was selected from seedling descendants of Yunnan large-leaf tea.

Used for both black and green tea.
history: Selection ran from 1974 to 1987. It was named a Jiangsu improved variety in 1987 and passed national approval in 1994 under number GS13006-1994. It grows in Wuxi, Yixing and Yizheng, with trial planting in Anhui, Hunan, Shandong and Henan. It stands up to cold and drought better than Fuding Dabai.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_wet: Elliptical leaves on a medium-sized, half-spreading plant, with moderately downy buds.
taste_profile: Expect what green teas usually give: fresh, vegetal and lightly sweet.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
